synopsis: MAPE is one of several metrics used to assess simulation agreement, specifically for sensor-signal models; other options include safety-quantity errors, time-history errors and distribution comparisons [f7553]. Sensor-model validation can apply MAPE to time-domain amplitude, point count and intensity, alongside separate checks of range accuracy, RCS correlation, attenuation and SNR [f4793]. Chapters 6 and 10 both report a 1.7% lidar signal-amplitude MAPE from independent on-road evidence published in 2022; Chapter 10 identifies the model as clear-weather automotive lidar [f4728, f7824]. Chapter 6 also reports 8.5% MAPE for point count and 9.3% for mean intensity, so the low amplitude error should not be treated as representative of every lidar output [f4728, f4729]. The cited numerical evidence is on-road, and these facts do not establish corresponding MAPE performance for heavy off-road machines or adverse weather [f4728, f4729, f7824].
